messages.author: bb723ef8c9a6e579
messages.subject: GAMMA REGRESSION
parts:
Dear INLA users,

I'm wondering if it is possible to fit a Gamma regression using the parametrization below:

Y_i \sim Gamma(alpha, beta)
log(alpha)= X gamma_1
log(beta)= X gamma_2

being gamma_1 and gamma_2 parameters corresponding to the fixed effects.

In particular, I'm interested in fitting a model like this:

Y_i \sim Gamma(alpha, 1)
log(alpha)= X gamma_1

Thank you so much,

Best wishes,
Joaquín.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] GAMMA REGRESSION
parts:
Hi,

the "gamma" likelihood is parameterised in a way that appears to not
match either the general or specific beta=1 case.

Further, the general case uses two predictors in one likelihood, so
isn't possible in the current implementation.

The special parameterisation of the precision (see the pdf on
r-inla.org, http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/doc/likelihood/gamma.pdf)
leads to (for a user-specified "scale" vector):
b[i] = scale[i] * phi / mu[i]^2
so that doesn't allow fixing beta.
However, since scale can be different for each observation, an
iterated approximation may be possible, similar to the inlabru
approach.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] GAMMA REGRESSION
parts:
On second thought, looking at the example in gamma.pdf, this may be
even harder, since "b" is the scale parameter and "a" is the _shape_
parameter.
What's your specific reason for wanting to fix beta and estimate alpha
only, as opposed to estimating the expectation directly?

Finn
